paragraphs.source_en: Benefits and Support/Approval The most positive relationship to emerge from Linda Marsh's study of Features, Advantages, and Benefits is the strong link between giving Benefits and receiving expressions of approval or support from custom ers. She found that the more Benefits the sellers gave, the more approv ing statements their customers made. This isn't a surprising finding. Af ter all, Benefits—as we define them—involve showing how you can meet an Explicit Need that the customer has expressed. Unless the cus tomer first says, "I want it," you can't give a Benefit. It's no wonder that customers are most likely to express approval when you show you can give them something they want.
